headline: Recommended denying five sidewalk requests on Clover and Heard streets and removing a streetlight near 10 Ware St.
summary: Also recommended approval of a guardrail at 101 Plantation St., pending project design and funding, and honorary street names for Laurel, Hancock, and Piedmont streets. Recommended sidewalk repairs on Norfolk St. at an estimated $68,000.00, and held more than a dozen petitions, including resurfacing requests.

CITY OF WORCESTER
Tuesday, November 17, 2026
PUBLIC WORKS COMMITTEE
Esther Howland (South) Chamber
Convened: 5:00 P.M.
Adjourned: 6:29 P.M.
Nikolin Vangjeli
COMMITTEE MEMBERS
Chairperson Tony Economou
Vice Chairperson Satya B Mitra
Councilor John P Fresolo
Joseph M. Petty
MAYOR
CLERK OF THE CITY COUNCIL
www.worcesterma.gov
City Hall - 455 Main Street  Worcester, Massachusetts
Present Were: Chairperson Councilor Tony Economou
Councilor Satya B. Mitra
Councilor John P. Fresolo
Also: Councilor Luis A. Ojeda
Councilor Jose A. Rivera
Councilor Robert A. Bilotta
Commissioner of Public Works John K. Westerling
Assistant Commissioner of Engineering Jay Mello, 
participated in the meeting remotely
Deputy City Clerk Stephen A.J. Pottle, clerk
. Virtual Attendee Call-In Information/Important Notice to Residents 1 
Pursuant to Chapter 20 of the Acts of 2021 and in order to ensure active, public 
engagement, the City of Worcester currently allows for both in -person and remote 
participation at all City Council and Standing Committee meetings. To partake in the 
meeting, you may attend the meeting in -person within the meeting location, follow the 
below link to join via Zoom or dial the direct line as indicated. If you join a Zoom meeting 
by dialing in with a phone number, you can raise your hand by dialing *9.
Public Works Committee Zoom Link: https://worcesterma.zoomgov.com/j/1615992759
Public Works Committee Zoom Phone Number: +1 646 828 7666
Public Works Committee Zoom Access Code: 161 599 2759
a.
Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the impersonation 
of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting payments be made 
for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions. All official emails 
regarding your petition will come exclusively from an @worcesterma.gov email address 
(such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail on the City of Worcester’s official 
letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always include your specific application 
details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, and location. The City of Worcester 
will never request payments via wire transfer.
b.
. Approval of the Minutes 2 
Order - That the City Council Standing Committee on Public Works hereby approves the 
minutes of the Public Works Committee meeting on November 5, 2026.
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and moved for a roll call vote to adopt the item . 
Order adopted on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Construct Sidewalk Petitions 3 
November 17, 2026 Page 2 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Jose A. Rivera request sidewalk installation on Clover St. from South Ludlow 
St. to Heard St.
# 8j CC November 10, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and moved to take the item up collectively with items 
#3b through #3e.
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Deputy City Clerk, who spoke concerning the 
process related to notifying abutters who may incur costs associated with sidewalk construction, the 
forty-three (43) public notices with non -binding ballots sent out to abutters of the area, including 
information related to receiving twelve (12) returned ballots with one (1) voting in favor of the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the following Speakers:
1. Nicholas Dupuis, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to the items
2. Michael Sullivan, Worcester resident, spoke in opposition to the items
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Rivera, who spoke in opposition to the items. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who discussed the cost of sidewalk 
construction being assessed to abutters with an estimated cost of $55.00 per linear foot with the 
Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the process relative for corner lots to be assessed to 
receive a corner lot adjustment with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who discussed surveys performed by 
the Department of Public Works (DPW) to assess the conditions of Clover St. and Heard St. for 
sidewalk construction, an estimated cost of $55,500.00 to construct sidewalks on Heard St. from 
Clover St. to Cowden St ., an estimated cost of $70,000.00 to construct sidewalks on Clover St. from 
Pine View Ave. to Heard St ., an estimated cost of $58,000.00 to construct sidewalks on Clover St . 
from Pine View Ave. to Mohawk Ave, an estimated cost of $49,700.00 to construct sidewalks on 
Clover St. from Mohawk Ave. to South Ludlow, and the eleven (11) received ballots in opposition to 
the item with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering and Deputy City Clerk. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who moved to recommend the items 
be denied. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the items be denied. 
Recommend Deny on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
November 17, 2026 Page 3 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Jose A. Rivera request sidewalk installation on Clover St. between Heard St . 
and Pine View Ave.
# 9f CC March 10, 2026
b.
Recommend Deny on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays (See Item #3a)
Julie Goering request installation of a sidewalk on Clover St. from Mohawk Ave. to Heard 
St.
# 7b CC February 4, 2025
c.
Recommend Deny on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays (See Item #3a)
Julie Goering request sidewalk extension on Clover St. from Mohawk Ave. to Heard St.
# 8f CC October 12, 2022
d.
Recommend Deny on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays (See Item #3a)
Councilor Etel Haxhiaj request installation of sidewalks along the length of Heard St ., and 
for a continuation of sidewalks from Pine View Ave. to Clover St ., with a cost estimate for 
said installations.
# 8c CC June 27, 2023
e.
Recommend Deny on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays (See Item #3a)
. Honorary Street Name Petitions 4 
November 17, 2026 Page 4 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Khrystian E. King and Councilor Robert A. Bilotta request Laurel St. from 
Summer St. to Everett Gaylord Blvd. be given the honorary street name designation of 
Arries Ann Ward Way.
# 8b CC September 22, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Gordon Ward, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
2. Idella Hazard, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Ojeda, Councilor Rivera, Councilor Bilotta , 
Councilor Mitra, and Councilor Fresolo, who highlighted the importance of celebrating community 
and preserving the city’s history as relates to the impacts made by Arries Ann Ward. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend approval of the item. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
November 17, 2026 Page 5 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Khrystian E. King and Councilor Luis A. Ojeda on behalf of Mayra Callahan 
request Hancock St. from Main St. to Hollis St. be given the honorary street name 
designation of Juana and Daniel Candelario Way.
# 10u CC September 8, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Luis (no last name provided), Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
2. Shelitza Betancourt, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
3. Mayra Callahan, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
4. Luceniz Gonzalez, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
5. Ayla Callahan, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
6. Katie Fleming, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
7. Steven Gonzalez, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
8. Maria Rivera, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou provided condolences to the family. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Ojeda, who highlighted the testimony 
provided by the family as relates to how Juana and Daniel would welcome the community into their 
home and the importance of honoring them by designating an honorary street in their names.
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved to amend the honorary street name designation to be Juana 
and Daniel Way.
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved as 
amended. 
Recommend Approval as Amended on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Mayor Joseph M. Petty and Councilor Luis A. Ojeda request Piedmont St. from Jaques 
Ave. to Davis St. be given the honorary street name designation of Meanes "Moe" 
Mooradian Way.
# 10x CC September 8, 2026
c.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized Councilor Fresolo, who spoke 
concerning the impact Moe Mooradian had and the legacy his son, Arthur, continues in the Piedmont 
St. neighborhood. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who spoke in favor of the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
November 17, 2026 Page 6 of 17Public Works Committee
. Guardrail Petitions 5 
Rich Perry request installation of a guardrail at 101 Plantation St. located at the 
intersection of Bleeker St. and Plantation St.
# 7c CC September 29, 2026
a.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speaker:
1. Rich Perry, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who 
provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) recommendation to install 
bollards and/or guardrail at the location, pending project design and funding. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to approve the item, pending project 
design and funding. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Tonya Gaston request the wall at the dead end of Ingalls St. be torn down and replaced 
with a guardrail.
# 8g CC July 15, 2025
b.
In Committee September 24, 2025 - Held
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering, who provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) 
recommendation to grant the item leave to withdraw, as the Massachusetts Department of 
Transportation (MassDOT) installed the wall to prevent cars traversing Ingalls St. from entering 
I-290, highlighted the petitioner’s concern about illegal activity in the area and provided an additional 
recommendation to report illegal activity to the Worcester Police Department (WPD). 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be granted Leave 
to Withdraw. 
Recommend Leave to Withdraw on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Miscellaneous Petitions 6 
November 17, 2026 Page 7 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Tony Economou on behalf of the residents of the Winter Heights 
Neighborhood request the granite survey markers that stick out of the sidewalks, some six 
to nine inches high, be cut down to pavement level, in the interest of public safety.
# 8a CC September 22, 2026
a.
Chairpreson Councilor Economou read the item and discussed the increasing amount of granite 
survey markers reported in neighborhoods with newer subdivisions around the city and an update 
relative to proposing the establishment of a process to remove protruding concrete survey markers 
as a potential Fiscal Year 2028 (FY 28) capital budget project with the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held. 
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Councilor Robert A. Bilotta request the southern portion of the fencing at Harrington Field 
Playground, located at 720 Franklin St., be extended to improve safety at the location.
# 10k CC September 8, 2026
b.
Chairpreson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the Assistant Commissioner of 
Engineering, who provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) 
recommendation to hold the item, as additional communication with the Department of Parks , 
Recreation and Cemetery (DPRC) is required to determine the ownership of the fencing with the 
Commissioner of Public Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be held. 
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
November 17, 2026 Page 8 of 17Public Works Committee
Julie Ann Lamacchia request review of the sidewalk on the western side of Burncoat St . 
between Arbutus Rd. and Rollinson Rd. to explore any warranty provisions and pursue

sidewalk was in Fall of 2024.
# 8f CC March 17, 2026
c.

Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Streetlight Petitions 7 
Councilor Jose A. Rivera on behalf of Rosemary McCarthy request installation of a 
streetlight at the intersection of Circuit Ave. East and Ferdinand St.
# 10m CC September 8, 2026
a.
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays (See Item #6c)
November 17, 2026 Page 9 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Jose A. Rivera on behalf of Sheila Loughnane request removal of the streetlight 
in the vicinity of 10 Ware St.
# 8q CC August 18, 2026
b.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speaker:
1. Sheila Loughnane, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed in the event the streetlight located in the vicinity of 10 
Ware St. were to be turned off the nearest streetlight being located approximately two hundred fifty 
feet (250’) away which would cause a significant illumination decrease resulting the possibility of 
decreasing public safety in the area and the streetlight being city owned with the Assistant 
Commissioner of Engineering and Commissioner of Public Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Fresolo, who discussed only the petitioner 
being notified for the item and the process related to sending public notices for streetlight petitions 
with the Deputy City Clerk. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Rivera, who spoke concerning efforts made 
to speak with the constituents on the street who have been affected by the streetlight’s illumination 
and provided resident approval to remove the light. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Mitra, who spoke concerning the item. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
. Sidewalk Repair Petitions 8 
Councilor Robert A. Bilotta request the sidewalk on the southern side of Temple St. be 
repaired.
# 10l CC September 8, 2026
a.
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays (See Item #6c)
Councilor Khrystian E. King request sidewalk repair on Rowena St.
# 10p CC September 8, 2026
b.
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays (See Item #6c)
November 17, 2026 Page 10 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Khrystian E. King request sidewalk repair on Brandon Rd.
# 10n CC September 8, 2026
c.
Recommend Hold on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays (See Item #6c)
Idella Hazard request sidewalk resurfacing in front of 75 Providence St.
# 8u CC August 18, 2026
d.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speaker:
1. Idella Hazard, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who 
provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) recommendation to grant 
the item leave to withdraw, as the utility work done at the location is within the jurisdiction of 
National Grid with the intent to replace the temporary patch with a permanent patch in the spring.
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the history of improper utility work performed 
throughout the city and the importance of holding contractors accountable for their quality of work. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou brought forth the following Chairman’s Order: “Request City 
Manager request Commissioner of Public Works work with National Grid to expedite permanent 
repairs to the sidewalk in front of 75 Providence St.”
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be granted Leave 
to Withdraw. 
Recommend Leave to Withdraw on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
Chairman's Orders
Request City Manager request Commissioner of Public Works work with National Grid to 
expedite permanent repairs to the sidewalk in front of 75 Providence St.
November 17, 2026 Page 11 of 17Public Works Committee
Vilson Castelo Branco request sidewalk repairs on Norfolk St. from Suffolk St. to Groton 
Pl.
# 9h CC August 18, 2026
e.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized the following Speaker:
1. Vilson Castelo Branco, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed the condition of the existing sidewalks with Speaker #1. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who 
provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) recommendation to add the 
item to the Sidewalk Repair List with the estimated cost of $68,000.00 associated with reconstructing 
sidewalks on Norfolk St. from Suffolk St. to Groton Pl.
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend the item be approved. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
November 17, 2026 Page 12 of 17Public Works Committee
Councilor Jose A. Rivera on behalf of Bill Metterville request sidewalk repair in front of 
Worcester State University, located at 486 Chandler St.
# 7h CC July 21, 2026
f.
Chairperson Councilor Economou read the item and recognized Councilor Rivera, who shared 
testimony in favor of the item provided by the petitioner. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering, who 
provided an overview relative to the Department of Public Works’ (DPW) recommendation to grant 
the item leave to withdraw, as a proposed project is scheduled in the area which would include 
sidewalk repairs at the location. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou recognized Councilor Rivera, who spoke concerning a feasible plan 
to repair the sidewalk in the event the proposed project be discontinued and an estimated cost of over 
$500,000.00 associated with reconstructing the sidewalks which exceeds the allotted budget for 
District Councilors to select items from the Sidewalk Repair List every two (2) years with the 
Assistant Commissioner of Engineering. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou discussed, in the event the proposed project be discontinued, the 
feasibility of splitting the sidewalk repair in the area into smaller portions to select for the purpose of 
lowering the costs associated with the repairs and the feasibility of DPW performing temporary 
emergency repairs with the Assistant Commissioner of Engineering and Commissioner of Public 
Works. 
Chairperson Councilor Economou moved for a roll call vote to recommend approval of the item. 
Recommend Approval on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
November 17, 2026 Page 13 of 17Public Works Committee
Lawrence O. Freed request sidewalk repair on Mill St. from 503-505 Mill St. to Logan

g.

discussed the new construction project on Mill St. and provided an overview relative to the 
Department of Public Works’ (DPW) recommendation to add the item to the Sidewalk Repair List.
